fields.actual_behavior: The cross-account fixture observation returns 200 with the owner account's invoice metadata, while the nonexistent-record control returns 404.
fields.expected_behavior: A non-owner should receive 403 or a uniform 404 without another account's invoice attributes.
fields.impact: Illustrated confidentiality impact: a user with one known invoice identifier can read another test account's owner identity and invoice amount. The example establishes only a simulated single-record read; bulk extraction, write access and live-system impact are not demonstrated.
fields.prerequisites:
Two synthetic accounts with separate sessions: Account A owns the invoice; Account B does not.
Known fixture invoice inv_demo_A_001. No enumeration or live requests are needed for this example.
fields.remediation: Resolve the invoice through the authenticated principal's permitted records, enforce ownership on the server, and add owner/non-owner/nonexistent-record authorization regression checks.
fields.sample_notice: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE / OFFLINE FIXTURE. No real target was tested; not a real program submission.
fields.steps_to_reproduce:
1. In the fixture, simulate GET https://api.reports-demo.invalid/api/invoices/inv_demo_A_001 as Account A using Authorization: [TOKEN_3]
2. Change only the session to Account B: Authorization: [TOKEN_5]
3. Compare the fixture attributes: both observations contain inv_demo_A_001, owner [EMAIL_1], amount 1200 USD, and one record.
4. As Account B, simulate a request for inv_demo_missing_999. The control returns HTTP 404 without invoice attributes.
fields.summary: Offline synthetic example: Account B ([EMAIL_2]) can read invoice inv_demo_A_001 belonging to Account A ([EMAIL_1]) by changing the invoice identifier. A nonexistent identifier returns 404. All statuses and invoice attributes are generated fixture data.
fields.title: [SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE] Cross-account invoice disclosure through a missing ownership check
